Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed: `eth0` is still at `172.20.10.123/24` (authenticated VLAN), never having moved to pre-auth, matching all prior occurrences exactly.

**Root cause:** Live inspection of `/persist/status/nim/DevicePortConfigList/global.json` on the paused device shows the same PNAC-disable/DPC-fallback oscillation: the new cycle-1 DPC (`TimePriority 01:48:30`, `PNAC.Enabled:false` — the disable/pre-auth-VLAN step) has `LastSucceeded: 0001-01-01` and permanently fails with "All attempts to connect to adam.evetest:443 ... src IP 172.20.20.123 ... context deadline exceeded" because it can't reach the controller once moved to the pre-auth VLAN. `dpcmanager` is therefore pinned at `CurrentIndex:1` on the stale prior DPC (`TimePriority 01:46:02`, still `PNAC.Enabled:true`, `CertEnrollmentProfileName:"new-scep-profile"`), which now fails with "No certificate enrollment status found for SCEP profile \"new-scep-profile\"" since the enrolled cert was already removed earlier in the cycle. Live `ip -4 addr show eth0` confirms the interface is still at `172.20.10.123/24`, the authenticated VLAN — it never moved — so the test's 3-way `Eventually` (cert removed + PNAC disabled + pre-auth VLAN) can never be satisfied and times out at 300s.

This is the identical mechanism already documented in this same run's `live-investigation.md` for `TestPNACWithoutProxy` — same two DPC entries, same errors, same stuck `eth0`. Per `live-ledger.md`, this exact PNAC-disable/DPC-fallback oscillation is a long-standing, unresolved, known/recurring issue affecting `TestPNACWithProxy`/`TestPNACWithoutProxy` on nearly every nightly run since it was first identified on 2026-11-17 — tonight is a continuation of that same bug, not a new regression.

Claude's conclusion:
This confirms the exact same known failure mode previously documented for run #57 on 2026-11-26.

**Root cause:** Live inspection of `/persist/status/nim/DevicePortConfigList/global.json` shows `dpcmanager` stuck at `CurrentIndex:1`, the older DPC (`TimePriority 01:08:53`, `PNAC.Enabled:true`, `CertEnrollmentProfileName:"new-scep-profile"`), rather than the newer cycle-1 disable DPC (`TimePriority 01:11:35`, `PNAC.Enabled:false`). The new disable-PNAC DPC has `LastSucceeded: 0001-01-01` and perpetually fails with "All attempts to connect to adam.evetest:443 ... src IP 172.20.20.123 ... context deadline exceeded" — it can't reach the controller from the pre-auth VLAN to validate. So `dpcmanager` falls back to the stale PNAC-enabled DPC, which in turn now fails with "No certificate enrollment status found for SCEP profile \"new-scep-profile\"" because the enrolled cert was already removed as part of the disable cycle. `ip addr show eth0` confirms the interface is still on `172.20.10.123/24` (the authenticated VLAN), never moving to pre-auth, so the test's combined `Eventually` (cert removed + PNAC disabled + pre-auth VLAN) can never be satisfied and times out at 300s.

This is the identical mechanism documented in `live-ledger.md` for the prior run (2026-11-26, run #57), and per that entry it's a long-standing, unresolved, known/recurring issue affecting `TestPNACWithoutProxy`/`TestPNACWithProxy` in nearly every nightly run since first identified on 2026-11-17 — tonight is a continuation, not a new regression. No PR diff was supplied, so no relatedness verdict is given.

This confirms the exact same known failure mode previously documented for run #57 on 2026-11-26.

**Root cause:** Live inspection of `/persist/status/nim/DevicePortConfigList/global.json` shows `dpcmanager` stuck at `CurrentIndex:1`, the older DPC (`TimePriority 01:08:53`, `PNAC.Enabled:true`, `CertEnrollmentProfileName:"new-scep-profile"`), rather than the newer cycle-1 disable DPC (`TimePriority 01:11:35`, `PNAC.Enabled:false`). The new disable-PNAC DPC has `LastSucceeded: 0001-01-01` and perpetually fails with "All attempts to connect to adam.evetest:443 ... src IP 172.20.20.123 ... context deadline exceeded" — it can't reach the controller from the pre-auth VLAN to validate. So `dpcmanager` falls back to the stale PNAC-enabled DPC, which in turn now fails with "No certificate enrollment status found for SCEP profile \"new-scep-profile\"" because the enrolled cert was already removed as part of the disable cycle. `ip addr show eth0` confirms the interface is still on `172.20.10.123/24` (the authenticated VLAN), never moving to pre-auth, so the test's combined `Eventually` (cert removed + PNAC disabled + pre-auth VLAN) can never be satisfied and times out at 300s.

This is the identical mechanism documented in `live-ledger.md` for the prior run (2026-11-26, run #57), and per that entry it's a long-standing, unresolved, known/recurring issue affecting `TestPNACWithoutProxy`/`TestPNACWithProxy` in nearly every nightly run since first identified on 2026-11-17 — tonight is a continuation, not a new regression. ### Root cause

Live inspection of `upgrade-app` (`6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c`) across all three nodes shows it's healthy, just not where the test is polling. On `edge-dev1` its `app-info` history ends in two consecutive `state:INITIAL` entries (no more BOOTING/RUNNING events after ~748236s), while `edge-dev3`'s `app-info` shows the same app reached `state:RUNNING` with pod IP `10.11.12.2` just afterward (`bootTime:1795748319`). This is the classic rolling-upgrade VMI eviction pattern: `edge-dev1` was cordoned/drained/rebooted for its baseos upgrade, the VMIRS evicted the app from it and rescheduled it onto `edge-dev3`, but the test's fixed SSH target (`cluster_upgrade_test.go:191`) kept polling `edge-dev1`'s `172.20.20.226:2222`, which genuinely has nothing listening for the app anymore — hence the 902s timeout.

This is the same mechanism already documented once before in the ledger under `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` (SSH-reach timeout against `edge-dev1:172.20.20.226:2222`, app actually relocated to `edge-dev2` in that case) — attributed there to a harness gap (fixed-device polling instead of resolving the node currently hosting a migrated app), similar to a recurring `FindDeviceHostingApp` bug seen for a different test. It is not one of the other previously-logged `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` failure modes (k3s single-node-bootstrap race, Proxmox `qmcreate` ZFS-lock timeout) — those have different signatures. Broker status shows the host at 105% memory overcommit but swap usage is low (0.5/8 GiB), so this doesn't look environment-driven tonight. No PR diff was supplied for this investigation.
